facts.text: B6 was a juvenile about four months old (USGS; some press say five).
B6 left Alaska on Oct 13, 2022 and landed in Tasmania on Oct 24 (UTC).
The flight lasted 11 days and 1 hour without landing.
At least 13,560 km nonstop.
USGS biologists tagged juvenile godwits on the Seward Peninsula near Nome in summer 2022.
5 g solar-powered satellite tag.
The bird carried leg flag B6.
Tags came off two other tagged chicks and kept transmitting from the ground.
Adults leave Alaska weeks before juveniles; juveniles migrate without adults.
Juveniles stage on coastal mudflats of western Alaska (Kuskokwim/Yukon deltas) before departure.
Before departure fat can exceed half of body mass; diet includes clams, worms, berries.
Digestive organs shrink and flight muscles and heart enlarge before departure.
Female E7 flew ~11,680 km Alaska to New Zealand in ~8.1 days in 2007, first tracked nonstop crossing.
Godwits cannot rest on the sea (no webbed feet), so must fly nonstop over the ocean.
Adult godwits time departures to favorable winds over the whole route.
Route: Aleutians, west of Hawaii, Kiribati (~Oct 19), Vanuatu, New Caledonia.
Alaska godwits winter in New Zealand and eastern Australia.
B6 passed ~600 km off Sydney, reached NZ latitude ~1,500 km west of it, and turned west toward Tasmania on Oct 23.
A researcher suggested strong easterly winds may have pushed it west.
How often juveniles take this route is unknown.
Previous record: adult male 4BBRW, ~12,200 km (2020).
B6 landed at Ansons Bay, northeast Tasmania.
It likely lost about half of its body weight (researcher estimate).
Sleep in flight has not been measured in godwits.
13,560 km in 265 h is ~51 km/h average (our calculation).
Along the approximate route, GFS wind at ~850 hPa helped ~9 of 10 hours, ~20 km/h mean, strongest north, weakest near equator (our analysis).
At the turn on Oct 23 morning the model wind was mostly from the north; NE winds later that day (our analysis).

calculations.question: How much did the wind help along the route?
calculations.method: Approximate route rebuilt from published waypoints (13,087 km smoothed); GFS 1-degree analyses every 6 h, wind at ~850 hPa (~1,500 m) projected on the flight direction (project analysis, Nov 2026)
calculations.result: Tailwind component positive ~9 of 10 hours; mean ~20 km/h; strongest north, weakest near equator

calculations.question: Did wind push it west at the turn?
calculations.method: GFS analysis at the turn area, Oct 23 00-06 UTC
calculations.result: Wind mostly from the north (pushing south); NE winds arrived later that day

conclusions.statement: The wind explains the overshoot better than the westward turn.
conclusions.counterpoint: Route is approximate; GFS 1-degree resolution is coarse.
